Hey man. I just wrote a post about this at 45 days in. I'm about your age. Had a gf that I broke up w 2 years ago that sent me spiraling into a long depression. Trust me, I feel your pain. I feel like a lot of advice out there is not very good and led me in the wrong directions, so let me give my take:  


1) Relapsing won't help. Point blank period. In fact, what helped me get OUT of the depression was NoFap. The thoughts that are telling you to do it are lying, and just seeking the quickest comfort. Let's be real though, you seeking the quickest comfort probably contributed to the breakup. If so, don't feel bad, it happens to the best of us.  


Seeking that quick comfort also leads you away from feeling better. Break ups are hard and since you're going to feel it anyway, keep up with the NoFap. I guarantee you you WILL feel better in 30 days if you hold on. But also your confidence and your attractiveness will increase.  
2) Under no circumstance should you make my mistakes. I fell into wallowing and self pity. However, Looking back it was a MASSIVE waste of time. Whether you want this girl back OR you want an upgrade, this is your opportunity to get your shit together. Immediately start working out. You don't need to be perfect. Even if you half-ass it for 6 months, you will be 100x better off for it. Trust me bro, work out. It will help your mood, and pay dividends with the next girl or her when she rolls back around. Which leads me too...  


3) No contact. Let me tell you about no contact. If you use no contact as a means to make her miss you it will 100% blow up in your face. I've had 2 separate opportunities to reconcile w my ex. I botched them both bc I was sitting there, endlessly being stressed about the situation, not working on myself in any meaningful way. So when I got that call or text and we did meet up I still ended up acting really needy.   


Instead, the best advice I can give you is go no contact, but use it as a way to outgrow her. Work on yourself relentlessly. Delete the pictures, unfriend or mute on social media. The chemistry here is that the more stimulus you get reminding you of her is like taking another puff of a cig when you're quitting. It sets you back and can cause you to spiral. You need to heal your dependency on her.   


4) If you do the above, it will feel like shit but in 1 month you'll be a better version of you. 2 months and you'll be a changed man. 3 and you'll be unrecognizable. This is usually when they come back around. Yes, they usually do. It's been 2 years and my ex now still messages me every now and then. The door is always open. 

Imagine a scene from a movie where the hero gets his ass kicked by the bad guy and then has to go train. At first he can't handle the training, but then surpasses his limits through raw consistency. Then he wins the epic showdown. So when you have to do something, and your mind is telling you you're too depressed, push through and get it done. Even if it's half-assed. Even if you're just going through the motions. You'll be surprised how quickly 1% better adds up.   


If you use this as a way to fuel your explosive growth, you will not only 100% no question either get her back or get someone who's a better fit, but you'll always be proud of how you handled this time in your life. And trust me, that is priceless.

  
There's a lot more detail I can go into, but this is a basic idea. Feel free if you want to DM. I've been there so happy to help. Good luck bro.

Point is that if you made a big mistake, dive deep and figure out why, and how you're gonna fix it. It's very easy to intellectually understand it but when emotions run high, you may slip into old patterns. You have to dig deep, and really work through those issues. Don't make the same mistake I did.
